title: Technical-instructions writing and blinded usability study
summary: Undergraduate teams write instructions for first-time Google Docs or Slides users, then test student- and ChatGPT-authored instruction sets without knowing their source. They submit instructions, usability notes, exit surveys, and a learning-assessment survey.

sources.title: Inviting ChatGPT into Technical Writing Classes: Opportunities, Challenges, and Student Perceptions
sources.evidence_quote: In the first classroom visit, students were randomly divided into teams of 3-5 to write a set of instructions.

course.name: Professional and Public Writing and Experience Architecture courses

assessment.summary: Write audience-centered software instructions and conduct blinded usability tests of human- and AI-authored documents.
student_actions: Write instructions for a first-time Google Docs or Slides user.
Rotate through user-tester, facilitator, and note-taker roles.
Test three or four instruction sets and identify usability problems.
Reflect on instruction writing and usability testing.

student_role.description: Students could not use additional resources while drafting. During testing, they critiqued documents that could be ChatGPT-authored without being told the source.

prohibited_actions: Use additional resources during the instruction-writing session
